about.title: Personal Injury Help in Parlier, California

In the most recent reported year, 16 injury collisions left 20 people hurt on local streets, with no traffic deaths recorded. Corridors like Manning Avenue, Academy Avenue, Parlier Avenue, and Mendocino Avenue see the highest volume of reported crashes, and public records show activity tends to cluster on Sunday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these incidents, or in any other kind of accident around town, you don't have to sort through insurance calls and medical paperwork by yourself. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured people in Parlier with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened. There's no cost to reach out, and if the attorney takes your case, you owe nothing unless there's a recovery. Time matters under California law, so it helps to ask questions sooner rather than later. We simply make the introduction; the decisions about your case are always yours.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Generally Have Two Years
items.desc: California law gives most injury victims two years from the date of the incident to file a claim. That window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved, so it pays to check early.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation is reduced by your share of fault rather than eliminated. Even if you think you contributed to what happened, you may still have a valid claim.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary personal injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This means compensation isn't artificially capped the way it is in some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That structure lets you get legal help without worrying about hourly bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: Most injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident date. If a government agency or vehicle was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Parlier?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Manning Avenue, Academy Avenue, Parlier Avenue, and Mendocino Avenue have the highest reported crash counts in town. Reported crashes also tend to peak on Sunday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply recorded counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, so being partially at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is instead reduced by your percentage of fault, which an attorney can help evaluate.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. If the attorney agrees to take your case, they work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In standard personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This is different from some other states that impose statutory limits on these types of damages.
